01.r: Hezekiah sent a message of surrender.
01.n: The verb has no object: 'sent' alone, meaning sent a message or messengers. The DRC adds 'messengers', as the Greek does. The 'and' that begins the verse is part of this word.

02.r: The king of Judah under Assyrian attack.
02.n: Gesenius: 'the might of Jehovah', a king of Judah, citing this chapter. The DRC follows the Greek and Latin form, Ezechias.

08.r: The Judean city where the Assyrian king was camped.
08.n: The name carries an ending of direction, 'Lachish-ward': the message went to Lachish. Gesenius: a fortified town in the plain country of Judah.

10.r: Hezekiah admits he broke faith with his overlord.
10.n: Gesenius: properly to miss, to err from the mark, as an archer does; from that, to sin. Here the wrong is against the king of Assyria, by rebelling. YLT keeps 'sinned'; most translations say 'offended'.

11.r: A plea that the Assyrian army leave.
11.n: A command form of the verb 'to turn back, return'.

12.n: Literally 'from upon me', as YLT's 'from off me' shows.

13.r: Marks what follows as the object of 'bear'.
13.n: This small word marks a definite direct object and has no English equivalent; it is counted here with 'what'.

14.n: BDB notes that this particle can include its own antecedent: 'that which'.

15.r: The amount the king will set.
15.n: The verb 'to give', used with 'on' in the sense to put or lay on. STEPBible tags this occurrence with the sense 'pay'. The tense is open: 'you will put', whatever it turns out to be.

16.r: As a load laid on Hezekiah.

17.r: Hezekiah promises to carry the burden, that is, to pay.
17.n: Gesenius: to take up, to lift up; the brief's lexicon gives bear, carry, endure. The tribute is pictured as a load; the BSB says plainly 'I will pay'.

18.r: The Assyrian king fixed the sum Hezekiah must pay.
18.n: Gesenius: to put, to set, to place, noting that in a related language it means to set a price. STEPBible's dictionary for this occurrence gives 'take', and its English gloss 'imposed'. The KJV says 'appointed', the BSB 'exacted'.

21.r: The sum is laid on Hezekiah as a burden.

25.r: Part of the number three hundred.

27.r: A large unit of weight for precious metal.
27.n: Gesenius: properly a circle or globe; the brief's lexicon: a round weight, talent. The word is singular after the number, as Hebrew counts.

28.n: Our register keeps 'silver' for this word. Gesenius: silver, so called from its pale colour.

29.r: The number of talents of gold.

30.r: The same weight, for the gold.

_extra.5: ἀγγέ(λους) (messengers): the Greek adds 'messengers' as the object of 'sent'; the Hebrew has none. The DRC follows it.
_extra.6: λους: the second part of the same word, split in the brief's Greek text.

10.n: ἁμαρτάνω, to sin, the usual New Testament word for sin, with the same root picture of missing the mark.

11.n: ἀποστρέφω, to turn away, turn back.

15.n: Dictionary form corrected; the brief gives only the preposition. ἐπιθῇς, 'you lay on', from ἐπιτίθημι.

18.n: ἐπέθηκεν, 'laid on', the same verb as 'you lay on' earlier in the verse.

25.n: τριακόσια, 'three hundred', one Greek word for the Hebrew 'three hundreds'.

27.n: τάλαντον, talent: the word our register renders 'talent' in the New Testament.

28.n: ἀργύριον, silver: the word our register renders 'silver' in the New Testament.
